title: Crash site regraded for soybeans after the documentary

tellings.quote: I even made a remark to James. James went there shortly after that. They had done land grading literally.

I would add is I'd like an explanation for why for 26 years not a single straw was removed from that place. Then after 26 years James' documentary comes out and they go there and remove more than 30 meters of earth.
tellings.difference: Says more than 30 meters of earth was removed after 26 years of the site being left untouched, and does not mention soybeans.
tellings.link_reason: Both tell of the Varginha crash site being dug up or regraded right after James Fox's documentary came out.

as_told.title: 30 meters of earth removed from crash site after James Fox documentary
as_told.place_text: Varginha crash site, Minas Gerais, Brazil

plain: A man named Carlos de Souza, interviewed by a podcast host, Jesse Michels, in an episode about a hospital that he says operated on an alien, talks about a spot near the town of Varginha in Brazil where something is said to have crashed. He says that for 26 years nobody touched the place, not a single straw. Then, he says, after a documentary by a filmmaker named James Fox came out, around 2022 or 2023, people went there and graded the land, removing more than 30 meters of earth. He mentions telling James about it, and says James went to see shortly afterward. Carlos is the only teller, speaking twice in one interview; the story's title says the land was cleared for soybeans, though in the quotes he does not mention soybeans. He says he would like an explanation, since it would suggest someone wanted the site wiped clean once attention returned to it.
